```{r}

```


```{r}
data <- read.table("result.csv", sep=",")
data$V1 <- as.factor(data$V1)
data$Type <- data$V1
data$Reconstruction <- data$V2
data$Reconstruction <- as.numeric(data$Reconstruction)
data <- data[c(3,4)]



```


# Histogramme


```{r}

ggplot(data, aes(x = Reconstruction, fill = Type)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, bins = 30) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("good" = "steelblue", "anomalie" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Histogramme des valeurs par type",
    x = "Valeur",
    y = "Fréquence",
    fill = "Type"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Reconstruction, fill = Type)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "dodge", bins = 30) 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("good" = "steelblue", "anomalie" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Histogramme des valeurs par type (comparaison côte à côte)",
    x = "Valeur",
    y = "Fréquence",
    fill = "Type"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Reconstruction, fill = Type, color = Type)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), position = "identity", alpha = 0.4, bins = 30) +
  geom_density(size = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("good" = "steelblue", "anomalie" = "firebrick")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("good" = "steelblue", "anomalie" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Histogramme et courbe de densité par type",
    x = "Valeur",
    y = "Densité",
    fill = "Type",
    color = "Type"
  )
```



```{r}
good_vals <- data$Reconstruction[data$Type == "good"]
anomalie_vals <- data$Reconstruction[data$Type == "anomalie"]



# Pour GOOD
hist(good_vals, probability = TRUE, col = "lightblue", main = "Distribution de GOOD", xlab = "Valeur")
lines(density(good_vals), col = "blue", lwd = 2)
curve(dnorm(x, mean(good_vals), sd(good_vals)), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# Pour ANOMALIE
hist(anomalie_vals, probability = TRUE, col = "salmon", main = "Distribution d'ANOMALIE", xlab = "Valeur")
lines(density(anomalie_vals), col = "red", lwd = 2)
curve(dnorm(x, mean(anomalie_vals), sd(anomalie_vals)), add = TRUE, col = "darkred", lwd = 2, lty = 2)


quantile(good_vals)
quantile(anomalie_vals)

# Ou des quantiles personnalisés
quantile(good_vals, probs = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99))
quantile(anomalie_vals, probs = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99))

```

#Le but dan sla suit est de dire quil ya une anomalie si au dessus du quantile 95%

```{r}

a <- quantile(good_vals, probs = 0.95)

anomalie_estimate <- data$Type[data$Reconstruction > a]

length(anomalie_estimate)

```





```{r}


a <- quantile(good_vals, probs = 0.55)
b <- quantile(good_vals,probs = 0.45)

anomalie_estimate <- data$Type[data$Reconstruction > a | data$Reconstruction < b]

length(anomalie_estimate[anomalie_estimate == 'good'])

```
